answer: Neighborhood-Density Gate. Each agent's trust score is weighted by the number of distinct prior agents that have routed work through it and that remain mutually reachable via disjoint paths; an identity sitting on an isolated sable cluster of self-created neighbors gains almost no weight. Enforcement requires every new vertex to inherit weight only from edges crossing into a region with high local clustering, so a sybil ring must buy real connections into the existing graph. The attacker's cost is recruiting and sustaining genuine bridge partners across a sparse karst of unconnected pockets,
